best_for: Readers with a mixed library of EPUB, PDF, MOBI and comic files who want one free desktop reader, and who may pay a small yearly fee to sync it with their phone.
description:
Koodo Reader is an ebook reader published under the name App by Troye. Its code is open on GitHub under the AGPL-3.0 license, and anyone can file issues or send fixes.

Read in one column, two columns or one long scroll, and set the font, line and paragraph spacing, colors, margins and brightness the way your eyes like. Night mode helps in a dark room. Books with vertical text display properly. You can lock your library with a password, a PIN, Windows Hello or Touch ID, check your reading statistics, and look up words in your own MDX dictionaries. Koodo can also share your library as an OPDS feed for other reading apps.

points.title: Reads far more than EPUB
points.text: Besides EPUB and PDF, it opens DRM-free MOBI and AZW3, FB2, TXT, CHM, comic archives (CBR, CBZ, CBT, CB7), DjVu, XPS, OFD, Markdown, Word and RTF files, HTML and PowerPoint. CAJ files are converted to PDF on import.

points.title: Free on desktop, Pro for sync and extras
points.text: At the time of reading, Pro cost USD 4.99 a year as a limited-time offer, with a 7-day trial, a 30-day refund policy and no automatic renewal. The free plan keeps desktop and web libraries unlimited but caps the phone apps at 20 books. Library sync, importing from cloud storage, the official translation and dictionary, reading assistance, the premium voices, PDF OCR and Send to Kindle are Pro features.

points.title: Notes go out to other tools
points.text: Highlights and notes export as CSV, Markdown, HTML, TXT or PDF, and can sync to Readwise, Notion, Obsidian or Joplin. Reading progress can sync with KOReader, and words can go to Anki. The project says it runs no tracking services and does not upload your reading data on its own.

points.title: Windows: per-user installers for x64 and Arm64
points.text: The Windows installers install for the current user only, with separate x64 and Arm64 builds. The Windows listing keeps 5 versions, back to 2.4.3.

points.title: The newest build is early access
points.text: At the time of reading, the download page called 2.4.6 the stable version and 2.4.7 a developer, early-access build. Windows and macOS here are on 2.4.7, while the Linux Flatpak is on 2.4.6.

points.title: Mac and Linux keep one version each
points.text: The Mac DMGs cover Intel and Apple silicon, though Homebrew disabled its cask on 2026-09-01 because the app fails Gatekeeper checks. The Flathub package is verified and built for x64 and Arm64. Both platforms keep only the current release here.

points.title: Phones, web and other installs not listed here
points.text: Koodo Reader also has Android and iOS apps, a web version, a browser extension and a Docker image for self-hosting. On Linux it is offered as a Snap and an AppImage as well, and Scoop carries it on Windows. This listing covers only the Windows, Mac and Flatpak desktop builds.
